Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: FAIL - The documentation.pdf contains a completely different paper ('The Dual-Route Model of Induction' about LLM copying behavior and concept/token induction heads) than what the plan.md describes (vector arithmetic in concept/token subspaces for word2vec-style parallelogram analogies). This fundamental mismatch prevents proper evaluation of whether conclusions match implementation results. While the plan.md stated results approximately match the cached experimental results (e.g., capital cities: claimed ~80%, actual 83.4%), the documentation is for an entirely different project.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: PASS - All experiments described in the plan are reflected in the implementation: (1) Building concept/token lenses from OV matrices (get_ov_sum function), (2) Capital Cities parallelogram arithmetic, (3) Family Relations parallelogram arithmetic, (4) Present Participle parallelogram arithmetic, (5) Past Tense parallelogram arithmetic, (6) Word2Vec tasks across all 14 categories, (7) Effective Rank analysis with rank sweep from 8 to 4096, (8) Comparison of four settings (raw, concept lens, token lens, all heads), (9) Using k=80 heads as specified. The scripts all_parallelograms.py, parallelograms.py, and parallelogram_ranks.py implement the methodology described in the plan.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: PASS - The reported effects have clearly non-trivial magnitude relative to baseline: (1) Capital cities: 83.4% (concept lens) vs 46.6% (raw) = +36.8 percentage points improvement, (2) Past tense: 85.4% (token lens) vs 31.9% (raw) = +53.5 percentage points improvement, (3) Present participle: 68.3% (token lens) vs 30.1% (raw) = +38.2 percentage points improvement. Most tasks show 10-50+ percentage points improvement over raw baselines. The concept lens excels at semantic tasks (capitals, family) while token lens excels at grammatical tasks (participles, past tense), as claimed.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: PASS - Key design choices have reasonable justification: (1) The OV matrix summation approach is explicitly based on prior work from Elhage et al. on transformer circuits, cited in the plan as 'induction heads identified in prior work', (2) The prefixes used (e.g., 'She travelled to' for geographic tasks) are explained in the CodeWalkthrough.md as disambiguating words and in code comments, (3) The layer sweep [0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 31] covers the full model depth appropriately, (4) k=80 heads is inherited from prior work on identifying concept/token induction heads. The methodology section in plan.md provides rationale for comparing four settings (raw, concept, token, all).
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: FAIL - Key experimental results are reported without appropriate measures of uncertainty or statistical significance: (1) No error bars or confidence intervals are shown in any plots, (2) Results are single accuracy values without standard errors or variance, (3) While sample sizes (n) are recorded in the JSON files (ranging from 506 to 4524 examples per task), no statistical tests are performed to verify significance of differences, (4) The parallelogram_analysis.ipynb plotting code does not include any error bar visualization, (5) No bootstrap confidence intervals or other uncertainty quantification is performed despite having per-example scores stored (ll_panswers, parallelogram_scores lists).
